scope: Web presentation optimization; not a native Elsword behavior claim

sources.evidence: Constructor registers at addMaterial; _markAllSubMeshesAsDirty scans every scene mesh but modifies only matching materials with prepared draw-wrapper defines. blockDirtyMechanism=false instead calls markDirty, another full scan. Cached-material and prepass invalidation are separate.
clone constructs a fresh SubMesh; its draw wrappers do not inherit the source's compiled defines. A fresh wrapper may exist, so safety is not based on an empty wrapper array.
Changing material resets that mesh's draw caches. Material context uniqueness is not assumed: WebGL may use undefined contexts.
isReadyForSubMesh creates defines before readiness can return false. The instance gate is removed before either readiness entry point is called.
clone still runs SerializationHelper.Clone and _clonePlugins with all original material values and texture rules.
instantiateModelsToScene remains unchanged, including the existing MultiMaterial source-subMaterials replacement behavior.
addMaterial/addMultiMaterial register synchronously; onNewMaterialAddedObservable is deferred. Releasing scene.blockMaterialDirtyMechanism dirties all materials and is not used.

bounds: Only the synchronous production instantiateModelsToScene call is wrapped.

Only newly registered instances with Babylon's original dirty method are gated; container source materials, their children, existing scene materials and custom dirty overrides retain their original path.
Unknown engine versions and nonconfigurable instance methods retain the unoptimized path.

Readiness calls restore the original methods before a plugin can prepare defines. If a plugin replaces either readiness entry, the next dirty request restores and executes the original scan while preserving the replacement; finally restores remaining descriptors on success, failure and nested calls.
No dependency/prototype patch, scene-wide blocking flag, geometry reduction, visual budget, material-value change or texture sharing change is applied.
Arbitrary plugins that manually inject draw-wrapper defines while bypassing material readiness are outside this production GLTF clone contract.

validation.headlessBoundary: NullEngine uses original geometry/material properties, omitting texture file I/O; separate synthetic tests cover ordinary texture cloning and shared render targets. Browser/GPU boot remains a separate acceptance check.
validation.result: 8 tests pass; baseline and optimized material serialization and first-frame defines match, including previously rendered source meshes, independent views, MultiMaterial sharing, morphs, prepass/plugin/cache side effects, existing dirty state, readiness-false invalidation, readiness-entry replacement, nested exceptions and exact descriptor restoration.

meshIterationExperiment.meaning: Visits through scene.meshes iterator during this one clone; not a claimed GPU frame time or full startup speedup.
